headline: Elected Wendy Pearl as Chair and David Ershun as Vice Chair, discussed project closeouts and the Girdler House generator issue.
summary: The committee discussed next steps on the Independence Park MOU audit process, deferring the audit to the next meeting. It elected new officers, reviewed closeout reports for the YMCA Shoe Shop and Cabot Theater projects, and discussed cost and gas line problems with the Girdler House Generator project. The committee also approved the April 16, 2026 meeting minutes as amended.
decisions: Elected Wendy Pearl as Chair of the CPC, 8-0.
Elected David Ershun as Vice Chair of the CPC, 8-0.
Approved the meeting minutes of April 16, 2026, as amended, 8-0.

4. Independence Park OOC_2024 – Discuss City Solicitor’s Opinion on next steps 29 
 30 
Regarding Independence Park, Beckwith explained that the Committee made a request to the 31 
City Solicitor's Office, to which they sent back a memo detailing various considerations. The 32 
Committee has requirements for milestones and invoices. A Committee member could review 33 
the invoices and supporting documentation to discuss it further with the Committee in terms of 34 
the MOU. If a project plans to undergo a significant change from what was foreseen at the time 35 
of application, the applicant could submit a formal memo to become part of the record. It would 36 
be a good idea to have a member of the Committee involved in the audits for review of the 37 
documents for the disbursement requests compared to the MOU.  38 
 39

the applicant needs to be held accountable for it. The Committee paid for public input, and this 41 
was received, but the Committee was never informed about any changes to come from that input. 42 
Any appreciable changes should be submitted clearly to the Committee.  43

 c. Girdler House Generator 93 
 94 
Beckwith explained that the Girdler House pulled together their electrician and plumber and met 95 
with a representative from National Grid regarding the generator to be powered with natural gas. 96 
The representative from National Grid reviewed the schematic plan, spoke with the plumbers, 97 
and reviewed the site, and gave the project the green light. During the connection of the fuel to 98 
the generator, a National Grid field representative reviewed the site and stated that it could not be 99 
done without a larger pipe coming in on a larger gas line. The electrician and plumber disagreed. 100 
National Grid does not have a high pressure system running through that area and so stated that a 101 
booster line would need to be installed. The original pipe would cost approximately $20,000 and 102 
the booster would cost approximately $37,500 additionally. Including all of the construction 103 
work needed, the project would likely total in the $70,000-$90,000 range. The Girdler House 104 
does not have that much funding. The Building Inspector suggested that something could be 105 
done in terms of the configuration of the unit and this is being discussed by the Girdler House 106 
internally. The Committee could make a formal recommendation to the Mayor's Office on this 107 
item asking them to reach out to National Grid to make this a priority. The Committee could also 108 
ask a representative from National Grid to attend a future meeting to discuss this further.  109 
 110
